label: first copy step (recall_idx 1) in short sequences (L=3, or L=4 with certain first tokens)
explanation: Sparse unit (about 0.24% of steps). About 90% of activation mass is at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1: input is orig(0) fed back, output is orig(1)), and almost all of it is in short sequences: L=3 (rate 6.6%, 52% of mass) and L=4 (39% of mass). It never fires at the delimiter step, at t<2, or at t>=7. The remaining ~10% is weak firing in the original phase at t=2-3 (to_go 1-2) on similar input tokens. Within the main context it is token-gated and graded: it is strongest when the fed-back first token is v/x/s/d/m (top examples are like v e g <DEL> [v] e) and when orig(1)/orig(2) are b/e/t/g/w/q/y. A single token set does not separate active from inactive cases cleanly, so precision stays low (the predicate is true on many inactive first-copy steps, especially with L=4). Does not fire for L>=5 except rarely (about 0.2x baseline rate).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (input phase: m, v, h, x; copy phase: x, v, m, l; delimiter step: ) and the next token to output (most: e, g, t, b, q, y; least: x, r, i, n); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, t=2, t=3.
